findings.body:
**Claimed critical; verifier found:** CHANGELOG.md’s Unreleased line claims an “API migration in scripts/pack.js”, but pack.js is absent on base and head, no source file imports tar-stream, and the diff only bumps package.json/lock to ^3.1.6—so the migration claim is false. Impact is a misleading changelog (no runtime consumer), so critical is too high.

The new Unreleased entry states that tar-stream 2→3 includes an "API migration in scripts/pack.js", and the PR description says call sites were migrated. That migration is not in this diff: `scripts/pack.js` does not exist on base or head, and no other source file changed.

tar-stream 3 changes pack/extract header and stream APIs relative to v2. If production code still uses the v2 call shape, installing `^3.1.6` will fail at runtime; if there is no consumer, this changelog line documents work that never shipped. Either include the `scripts/pack.js` (or other call-site) migration in this PR, or drop the migration claim until that change lands.

`tar-stream` moves from a v2 range (`^2.2.0`) to a v3 range (`^3.1.6`) with no other source edits in the PR. For a major upgrade, the diff should show the pack/extract call sites updated for the v3 API (the changelog even points at `scripts/pack.js`).

As landed, reviewers cannot verify that consumers compile or run against 3.x. Add the migrated call sites (or a brief note in the PR body if this package truly has zero runtime imports and the bump is lockstep-only for a downstream image).

summary:
## Verdict

Incomplete major upgrade — the version bump is present, but the claimed call-site migration is not.

## What changed

`tar-stream` is raised from `^2.2.0` to `^3.1.6` in `package.json`, with a matching `package-lock.json` pin to `3.1.6` and a CHANGELOG bullet under Unreleased. That is the entire diff (3 files, +3/−2).

## Why this is a problem

The PR description says call sites were migrated, and `CHANGELOG.md` names an API migration in `scripts/pack.js`. Neither base nor head contains `scripts/pack.js` (or any other consumer of `tar-stream`). A major bump of `tar-stream` changes pack/extract header and stream APIs; shipping only the version range without the migration the authors themselves document leaves the upgrade half-done and the release notes inaccurate.

`package-lock.json` is present and the locked version matches the manifest range, so lockfile drift is not the issue here.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
